newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares up as market confirms gains.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares up as market confirms gains.

text.p: Russian shares firmed on Monday led by Surgutneftegaz which rose on news of an ADR issue, traders said.
Monday was the first day of trade by both Western and Russian investors since November 6.
The Russian Trading System index rose to 188.74 from 186.07 on Sunday and from 184.35 on November 6.
The system saw a healthy $25 million volume, though some dealers said the market was playing catch-up after low holiday activity.

Loren Bough of Brunswick said the roughly three percent gain on November 6 showed that buyers were confirming new price levels after President Boris Yeltsin's successful bypass operation on November 5.
"During the intervening four days of holiday, news on Yeltsin has given the market a firm tone," he said, adding that the Eurobond road show was also a market stimulus.
Wall Street was open on Monday but activity was reduced for a U.S. holiday and brokers said they expected increased attention from the U.S. on Tuesday.
Russian markets were closed November 7 and 8 but open on Sunday, when Western markets were closed.

Surgutneftegaz, which announced it had signed a depositary agreement with the Bank of New York as part of plans to issue American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) rose to $0.4240 from $0.4080 on Sunday and $0.3965 on November 6.

The Federal Commission for the Securities Market also said it was examining a supplementary share issue by Surgutneftegaz, wholly taken up by majority shareholder Surgut Holding, after numerous inquiries from investors.
Surgutnefegaz common shares trade volume reached $7.7 million on Monday, more than the entire market traded on Sunday.
Some traders said Western investors were bullish but holding back from placing money in the market as they re-evaluated their portfolios.
"Generally people are going to be bullish for the next six months but if that will happen next week is hard to call," said Renaissance Capital dealer Victor Pitaleff.
Mosenergo traded late on Monday at $0.978, down from $0.993 on Sunday but almost flat on $0.979 on November 6. LUKoil traded at $10.60, down from $10.70 on Sunday but up from $10.38 on November 6.
Moscow City Telephone (MGTS) preferred, one of a number of preferred stocks which firmed on Monday, rose to $440.00 from $400.00 on November 6. It was not traded on Sunday.
